 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. New season, same old  Tim Hardaway ?
 For years, he has taken shots at the new generation in the NBA. So when Darius Acuff Jr. came up on "The Crossover Podcast," did he stick to that same line? Or was there a little more nuance to his latest remarks?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That is definitely worth a closer look.
 A rookie record nobody really wants  
 Acuff Jr.  has barely gotten a whiff of NBA air. Still, the Sacramento Kings' seventh overall pick out of Arkansas is already a record holder. Just not of a record you'd necessarily want.  
 Through his first three games, Acuff Jr. took 73 shots. That broke the previous mark of 64. It was set by Kevin Durant in his 2007-08 rookie season for the Seattle SuperSonics.
 When that very fact came up on the podcast, Hardaway counted off the attempts himself — 24, 26, 23 — before  blurting out ,  "Come on, man."   
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That only underlined what the five-time NBA All-Star had already made clear earlier in the episode. When somebody brought up Acuff Jr. as his Rookie of the Year candidate, Hardaway clearly wasn't having it.
 Volume shooting with little efficiency behind it 
 Hardaway started off by saying Acuff Jr. is shooting the hell out of the ball. Then Tim Bug caught himself and pivoted. What he really meant was that Acuff Jr. was just letting it fly. 
 High volume. Poor efficiency.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For the  Miami Heat  legend, that is not the way to go. The young  Kings  guard needs to  "distribute a little bit more." 
 After that, somebody in the studio asked exactly who Darius was supposed to pass to, implying that the Kings (for some, still the black hole of the league) have nobody who scores any better.
 Hardaway did not let that slide, though.
 He named center Domantas Sabonis and sharpshooter Malik Monk as players Acuff Jr. should look to a lot more. Zach LaVine, a two-time All-Star, deserves a mention here too.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Related: "I know of a girl who's with 10 different athletes a year" – When former NBA player revealed the secret world of athletes and groupies 
 Two eras of point guard play 
 Hardaway's opinion? It should not simply be brushed aside. 
 Tim is a Hall of Famer. He also played the same position Acuff Jr. plays now. Not too shabby at it, either.
 Back in 1990-91, Tim Bug ran the point for Run TMC in Golden State. Nearly  23 points and close to 10 assists  a night. That balance — scoring with anyone, yet knowing when to give the ball up — is a big reason the Chicago native is remembered the way he is today. Consequently, it makes sense that this exact balance is what he now misses in Acuff Jr. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Still, it is a little more nuanced than that.
 Right now, Acuff Jr. is not shining in much besides scoring. So letting him embrace exactly that with the green light might actually help him. It, in fact, is the kind of iso ball the league has leaned on plenty of times in recent years.
 Hardaway's days? They looked different. Offenses were much more built around team play back then. That might add to his remarks about the 19-year-old.
 Still, Darius has to be careful not to become too one-dimensional. Say he has better teammates in a few years. He cannot keep putting up  numbers  like these — 21.5 points on 34.4 percent shooting and 20.6 percent from three — while overlooking the guys around him. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That is a recipe for disaster. Even if the Kings are pretty much used to those by now.
